description.text: Pixels outside the input format are set to black.
Values in this channel are added to the size of the area to sample, to add extra blur or diffusion to the distortion.
Multiply the blur values by this.
The effect is applied only to these channels.

impulse:	no filtering - each output pixel equals some input pixel
linear:	linear interpolation between pixels
cubic:	smooth interpolation between pixels
Keys:	cubic a=.50, approximates sinc (*)
Simon:	cubic a=.75, continuous 2nd derivative (*)
Rifman:	cubic a=1.0, lots of sharpening (*)
Mitchell:	mix of sharpening and smoothing (*+)
Parzen:	approximating B-spline (+)
notch:	hides moiré patterns (+)
Lanczos4:	good for scaling down (*)
Lanczos6:	good for scaling down with some sharpening (*)
sinc4:	good for scaling down with a lot of sharpening (*)
(*) has negative lobes, can produce values that are outside the range of the input pixels.
(+) not interpolatory, changes pixels even when no movement.

This is the GPU that will be used for rendering, when Use GPU if available is selected. If you have more than one GPU in your machine, you can select a different GPU Device to use by editing your Preferences. (Note that selecting a different GPU will require a restart of Nuke to take effect.) Local GPU will be shown as Not available when any of the following is true: * Use CPU is selected as the GPU Device in your Preferences. * No suitable GPU was found on your system. Please refer to the documentation for details of the requirements for GPU acceleration. * It was not possible to create a context for processing on the selected GPU. For example, this can happen when there is not enough free memory available on the GPU. To use the GPU when rendering from the command line, add --gpu to your command.

Select this to render on the Local GPU, if available. You can select this even if no GPU is currently available on your machine. The GPU will then be used whenever the script is opened on a machine which does have a GPU available. You should also select this if you wish to render from the command line with the --gpu option. If this node requires full frames from its inputs, and is therefore unable to reduce its memory overhead, it will fall back to the CPU if an attempt to render a frame on the GPU fails due to lack of memory. When this occurs, a warning message will be printed to the console.

description.plain_text: C_STMap 2.1v5: Allows you to warp the src image according to the stmap or ppass map. An stmap has two channels U and V representing the absolute positions of the source pixels normalised between 0 and 1, where (0,0) is the bottom left corner of the input image, and (1,1) is the top right corner. A ppass has three channels X, Y, and Z representing the normalised 3D coordinates of the source image in latlong domain.
description.text:
C_STMap 2.1v5: Allows you to warp the src image according to the stmap or ppass map.

An stmap has two channels U and V representing the absolute positions of the source pixels normalised between 0 and 1, where (0,0) is the bottom left corner of the input image, and (1,1) is the top right corner.

A ppass has three channels X, Y, and Z representing the normalised 3D coordinates of the source image in latlong domain.
